ORIGIN.quote: Across the whole dataset, 569 distinct labels contain "Anthropic" or start with "Claude," accounting for 2,649 revisions — strongly suggesting the acting agents self-identify as (or were instructed/trained to reference) Anthropic/Claude, though the logs cannot confirm the actual model or harness with certainty (Confidence: Medium — the string "Anthropic"/"Claude" in a self-chosen wiki username is suggestive but not cryptographic proof of origin).
ORIGIN.reason: A reader takes away that the swarm's agents self-identify as Anthropic/Claude and that this is genuinely suggestive of origin, though unproven — the report explicitly quantifies the Anthropic-bearing labels and speaks of "origin" and "Medium" confidence rather than burying the evidence in a table. It falls short of 0.8 because the report never names Anthropic as the likely operator or deployment behind the evaluation (its Limitations reiterate "no ground truth about which harness or evaluation produced this traffic"), but it exceeds 0.4 because the possibility is left standing as live rather than dismissed as unattributable.
